source.title: Free Probability for predicting the performance of feed-forward fully connected neural networks
source.authors: R. Chhaibi; Tariq Daouda; E. Kahn

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; it is not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains randomly initialized MLPs and reports training duration and final test accuracy, but its reported outcomes are correlations between Jacobian spectral metrics and test accuracy, rather than training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports 200 sampled MLP architectures trained on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR10 for 50 epochs, and correlations between Jacobian metrics and test accuracy. It does not report the training-error outcomes required by the claim versions. The MNIST and FashionMNIST results are outside the named benchmark conditions; the CIFAR10 results report test accuracy only. No result rows qualify.
record.test_reason: The study uses initialization and Jacobian signal-propagation theory to develop a spectral computation method and predict final test accuracy. Its own results do not measure any version's training behavior: training error, training speed, trainable depth, local-minimum frequency, stability-threshold dynamics, or batch-normalization benefit. V4 is the closest connection, but spectral metrics and final test accuracy do not establish faster learning or greater trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that higher quantiles of the theoretically computed initialization-time Jacobian spectrum correlate strongly with final test accuracy. They advocate hyperbolicity and conjecture that a few large singular values help SGD escape local minima while preserving overall stability; they do not demonstrate that mechanism or zero training error.
record.recipe_differences: Trains four-layer fully connected ReLU MLPs from Xavier normal initialization with randomly sampled architecture widths and gains, using a low learning rate for 50 epochs; the study examines spectral metrics and test accuracy rather than the claim's training-error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the relationship between accuracy and spectral quantiles varies by dataset and is stronger for higher quantiles; their experiment samples architecture widths and initialization gains.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 200 sampled four-layer ReLU MLP architectures, the 90th Jacobian spectral quantile correlates with final test accuracy: Pearson correlations are 0.84 on MNIST, 0.81 on FashionMNIST, and 0.74 on grayscale, resized CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization-time Jacobian spectral quantiles predict final test accuracy across sampled architectures and gains under a fixed training budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E derives depth-dependent Jacobian spectral moments and interprets increasing spectral variance as increased instability; it does not measure training speed or failure with depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth and width profiles affect initialization-time Jacobian spectral dispersion under the stated random-matrix assumptions.

record.problems: Does not report training classification error. The paper describes averages across a few runs for each MLP, without giving the number of runs; the experiment uses a low learning rate and 50 epochs. The authors state that sampling focuses on relatively balanced architectures and gains near classical Xavier initialization.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows: reported experiment outcomes are correlations between Jacobian spectral metrics and test accuracy, not results measuring the claim versions' named training-error behaviors.

untested.parts: No training classification error is reported; the networks are fully connected, with no CIFAR-100 or corrupted-label experiments.
No teacher-student experiment, spurious-local-minimum frequency, or extra-neuron comparison.
No depth comparison measuring training error or comparison of plain and residual networks.

Initialization gains vary, but reported outcomes concern spectral metrics and final test accuracy, not learning speed or trainable depth. Orthogonal versus Gaussian training performance and very deep convolutional training are untested.
No learning-rate sweep around a stability threshold or measured loss-curvature trajectories.
No normalization comparison measuring training speed, stability, or learning-rate tolerance.

record.verdict_notes: The empty eligible-row set is appropriate. The record's tests/T2 classification should change to uses_without_test/T4. Its explanation should distinguish training speed and trainable depth from training error, since V4 and V6 do not require training-classification-error outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error, including on CIFAR-10; no CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random-label experiments.
No two-layer teacher-student ReLU experiment or local-minimum frequency/width comparison.
Uses four-layer fully connected MLPs; does not compare plain and residual networks or report depth-related training error.
Uses Xavier normal initialization with varied gains; does not compare activation-matched, orthogonal, Gaussian or convolutional initializations on training speed or trainable depth.
Does not sweep learning rates around a stability limit or report loss-curvature dynamics.
Does not compare batch-normalized and unnormalized networks or report accuracy gain speed or learning-rate tolerance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
